Numbers have always felt like the most visible part of storytelling: at the meeting point of shape, timing, and meaning. That curiosity about how people, events, and decisions come together is what drew me to a career as a Data Analyst, and it has grown into a clear commitment to turning raw data into insights that help organisations make smarter, more human-centred decisions. I am originally from Senegal, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my academic and professional journey, I have completed 8 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in work that connects evidence, strategy, and measurable impact. What keeps me engaged in this field is the chance to uncover patterns and trends in data quickly and turn them into recommendations that are clear, actionable, and useful for both users and teams.

My academic and professional path has also shaped how I approach complex work. In one role, I needed to use a technique that was new to me, learned it within a couple of months, and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value those moments because they often begin with a simple question and end with a clear answer. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when deadlines and revisions demanded it.

One of my favourite memories is bringing my family to a company open day, where they began pointing out the data being recorded and asked me to explain it in their own words. Seeing my family connect with the human story behind the numbers confirmed why this profession matters to me. I am now eager to bring this combination of curiosity, structured thinking, and practical problem-solving to a Data Analyst role where I can contribute to meaningful decisions and continue growing through work that helps organisations do more with less.

Clear reporting matters because it helps communities make sense of the world, and that belief is what drew me to journalism. What began as a routine assignment became a warm, personal conversation that showed me how closely reporting is tied to real relationships and shared experience. It also reinforced for me that journalism is not only about facts and accuracy, but about the stories people can see and hear without losing sight of the human thread.

My academic and professional path has also been shaped by practical experience. Across my work, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each requiring me to turn complex material into accurate, compelling stories that readers can quickly understand and trust. In one role, I had to learn a new technique the work required; within a couple of months I was using it independently in my own tasks. On another assignment, a recurring issue was slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value those moments because they reflect the collaborative side of journalism. During a lengthy stretch of work with several setbacks, I stayed with the project through each stage and added extra hours when deadlines demanded it so that the final deliverables were completed properly.

These experiences have strengthened my commitment to journalism, and I am ready to bring that same sense of purpose, rigour, and public focus to my next role.
